Late June 1944. The hills south of the Palel-Tamu road.
In early May the brigade attacked the airfield at Palel and was thrown back.
The Indian soldiers defending it did not come over. They fought.
Since then the brigade has held on in these hills, raiding British patrols and road-blocks.
Supplies are not coming.
More than half the brigade is sick or wounded.
Men have begun to slip away.
Your section is going out against one of the road-blocks.
The ground you are about to see is a test range, not the real place. Your section and this raid are fiction.
Source: Chandar S. Sundaram, "A Paper Tiger", War & Society 13:1 (1995), pp. 48-49. One source so far; this text may change.

How to play
Keys
Space pauses and resumes. Give your orders while paused.
1 and 2 select a team. Clicking one of your men selects his team.
Right-click sends the selected team to that spot.
Shift + right-click adds a further leg to its route.
F tells the selected team to hold fire, or to fire again.
B makes the selected team fall back to where it started. Men falling back go even when pinned, and do not fire.
R starts again. H shows this page. O shows the debug overlay.
What you are looking at
Circles are your men, marked with their team number. Diamonds are the enemy.
The bar over a man shows how much fire he is under. Past the white tick he is pinned: he stops walking and fires slower and worse. Red means he has broken and will not fire.
Dark green is thick jungle. Nobody can walk or see through it.
A brown bank is cover. A man within two cells behind it cannot be hit by fire that comes over it. Fire from the side still hits him.
A man who is walking does not fire.
Rounds are counted. A man with none left cannot fire.
